items.text: Identify the report as a scoping review.
Structured summary from background through conclusions.
Rationale in light of what is known; why a scoping review.
Questions and objectives framed by population, concept and context.
Whether a protocol exists, where, and registration details.
Eligibility criteria for sources of evidence, with rationale.
Information sources searched, coverage dates and last search date.
Full electronic search strategy for at least one database.
Process for screening and selecting sources of evidence.
Data charting methods, independence, and confirmation with investigators.
Variables charted, with assumptions and simplifications.
If done, rationale and methods of critical appraisal and its use.
Methods for handling and summarising the charted data.
Numbers screened, assessed and included, with reasons, ideally in a flow diagram.
Characteristics of each source of evidence, with citations.
If done, critical appraisal data within sources of evidence.
Charted data for each included source of evidence.
Charting results summarised against the review questions.
Main results, linked to the questions, and relevance to key groups.
Limitations of the scoping review process.
General interpretation, implications and next steps.
Funding of the included sources and of the review, and funder role.
